questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Republic of Ireland?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Republic of Ireland article.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Republic of Ireland?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Republic of Ireland on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Republic of Ireland article.

questions.proof: It shares a border with Northern Ireland (which is part of the United Kingdom).

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Republic of Ireland?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Republic of Ireland article.

questions.proof: The Irish language is widely taught in all schools, and it is still spoken as a first language in some areas of the country, known as the Gaeltacht.

questions.prompt: What money is used in Republic of Ireland?

hints.nudge: Money names often come from a country’s own words. The other three are spent in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Republic of Ireland article.

questions.proof: Ireland is a European country on the island of Ireland.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Unionists, who feared being ruled by Irish Catholics and losing their social and economic position, had grown in strength since _____.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the nineteenth century.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Home Rule Movement” part of the Republic of Ireland article.

questions.proof: Unionists, who feared being ruled by Irish Catholics and losing their social and economic position, had grown in strength since 1886.
